transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me. It's nice to meet you, too. 

I, um... well, I hope I'm doing this right, but my family wanted me to come in. I came in because... well, it's a little hard to admit, and I really don't want to sound dramatic or be a burden to anyone. But lately, I just keep thinking it would be... better, I guess, if I just didn't wake up. 

I'm sorry, is it okay that I say that? I know it sounds terrible. It's just... sometimes I feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family, and to my crew at work. I know I shouldn't think that way, and I'm really trying to be better, but I just thought I should probably talk to a doctor about it... if that makes sense?
Have you ever had a distinct period of feeling unusually elevated or irritable compared with your usual self?

Elevated? Um... like, really happy or full of energy? No, I don't think so. I'm sorry, I hope it's okay to say no to that. I mostly just feel... well, pretty down and heavy most of the time. 

And I really try my best not to be irritable with anyone. I know my crew at work relies on me, and my family does too, so I try really hard to keep a good attitude and not snap at people, even when I'm feeling awful. I don't want to make things harder for them than I already do. 

So, no, I don't think I've ever had a period like that... did I understand your question right?
Did these feelings begin after a particular stressful event or change in your life?

Well, yes, actually. I hope it's alright to share this, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining... but things got really hard about a year and five months ago. 

My husband, he... he had a really bad back injury, and it left him mostly housebound. It's been a huge adjustment for both of us, and I've really tried to be strong for him and keep everything going with my work installing floors, but... well, that's when this heavy feeling really started to settle in. 

I feel so guilty even saying it, because he's the one who was hurt, not me, and I should be doing a better job of handling it all. I'm sorry, I hope I'm not oversharing. Does that answer your question?
During the past two weeks, have you lost interest in or stopped enjoying things that you usually enjoy?

Well... I guess so, yes. I mean, I really try to keep up with things, I promise I do. I don't want to just let my life fall apart. But... lately, it's been hard. 

I used to do a lot of things that made me happy. I would paint, and I loved cooking big meals for my family. I even used to go for a run before my flooring jobs, and I was involved in local theater... I'd never miss a rehearsal. 

But now... I don't know, I hope this doesn't make me sound lazy or ungrateful, but those things just feel like chores now. Like they belong to somebody else's life, not mine. And... I don't even really care if I miss them anymore. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be trying harder to stay active and engaged. Is it normal to feel that way? I just feel terrible that I've let all those good things go.
During the past two weeks, have you been feeling unusually tired or low in energy?

Well... yes, I suppose I have been. I really try to push through it, I promise. I don't want my clients or my husband to think I'm slacking off, so I try to keep a smile on my face... but it's just been so hard lately. 

It's actually a little embarrassing to admit, but... by the time I carry just one box of tile onto a job site, or even just answer a couple of client messages, my body just feels like wet cement. And my head gets so tired that I can't even make simple decisions about the installation anymore. 

I hate being like this, I really do. I hope you don't think I'm just making excuses for being lazy. I really am trying my best to keep my energy up. Is it okay that I'm struggling with this so much right now?

{"intent":"Assess for a depressive-episode symptom that would help distinguish major depressive disorder from an adjustment disorder.","question":"During the past two weeks, how has your sleep been?""}

Well... my sleep has been... okay, I guess. I mean, I don't want to make a big deal out of it. I know everyone has trouble sleeping sometimes, especially when they're stressed. 

I've been trying really hard to stick to a good schedule, you know? Going to bed at a reasonable hour, trying not to look at my phone... but... I don't know, maybe I'm just not doing it right. I haven't really noticed a huge change, or maybe I'm just so used to being tired that I can't tell anymore. 

I hope that's an okay answer. I just don't want to complain about something if it's just normal stress, you know? Am I supposed to be keeping better track of how many hours I get?
During the past two weeks, have you noticed any change in your appetite?

Well... I guess my appetite has changed a little bit, but I don't want it to sound like I'm starving myself or anything like that. I really do try to eat, I promise. 

It's just that... most days, I guess I just sort of forget to eat until it's really late in the day. Or, if my husband makes something nice, I'll take a few bites and then I just feel kind of sick to my stomach. I don't mean to waste food, I really hate doing that. 

And... well, I have noticed that my work pants have gotten pretty loose lately. I haven't been trying to lose weight on purpose, it's just happening. I hope that's not a bad thing. Is it okay that I'm not eating as much right now? I really am trying to do better when I can.
When you think it would be better not to wake up, do you have any intention of killing yourself or a specific plan to do so?

Well... no, I don't have a plan or anything like that. I really don't want you to think I'm crazy or dangerous. I would never want to put my husband or my crew through something like that on purpose. 

It's just... that's actually why I came in today, to be honest. I just keep having these thoughts that it would be better if I didn't wake up. And... sometimes I feel like dying would just be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew. I've just been such a burden to them lately, and I feel so guilty about it. 

I know it's a terrible thing to say, and I'm so sorry if it sounds alarming. I'm not going to do anything, I promise. I just... I can't seem to stop the thoughts from coming. Is it normal to feel this way when you're just so tired of being a disappointment?
During the past two weeks, have you felt sad, empty, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day?

Well... I mean, I guess I have felt a little down lately. But I really don't want to sound like I'm just feeling sorry for myself, you know? Everyone has bad days, and I know I have so much to be thankful for. My husband is so patient with me, and I have a good job. 

I just... I don't know, it's like this heaviness that just kind of sits there, most of the day. And I do feel kind of empty, like I'm just going through the motions at work and at home. But I try really hard to put on a brave face so I don't bring anyone else down. 

I hope it's okay to admit that. I just feel like I should be able to snap out of it, and I'm really trying, I promise. Am I making too big a deal out of just being sad?
